title: Explore City Connectivity (DFS)
real_world_story: City engineers trace a route from a central facility deep into the neighborhood network before backtracking to explore alternate branches. Depth-First Search mirrors this deep exploration of the city's infrastructure.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Facilities and the roads or utility lines that connect them
real_world_connection.source_represents: The facility where the inspection begins
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following one branch of connections as far as possible before backtracking

problem_statement: Given N facilities numbered 0 to N-1 and E undirected connections, find the order in which facilities are visited starting from a given source S using Depth-First Search. Process neighbors in ascending index order.
task: Return the DFS traversal order of all facilities reachable from the source S.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain two integers u v describing an undirected connection between facilities u and v. The final line contains an integer S, the starting facility.
output_format: Print the DFS traversal order as space-separated facility indices.

examples.explanation: Starting at facility 0, DFS moves to 1, then 3, then 4 before backtracking to explore 2.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS dives deeply along one branch of connections before backtracking, which is useful for exploring the full reach of a connected city network.

hint: Mark a facility as visited when it is reached.
Recursively explore the neighbors of a facility before backtracking.
Process neighbors in ascending index order for a deterministic result.
real_world_takeaway: DFS is a natural way to explore a city network deeply along connected branches, helping engineers understand which facilities lie on each infrastructure path.
